passages.title: Designing Accessible Public Spaces
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of design, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Step-free routes can help wheelchair users, travellers with luggage and people with prams. Clear visual contrast can help people identify signs and edges.
Resting places are useful when distributed along longer walking routes. Tactile maps and indicators can support visitors with limited vision.
Designers should consult people with a range of access needs. Accessible features can become ineffective if they are not maintained.
Consistent signs help visitors navigate unfamiliar spaces. Access is usually easier to incorporate when considered at the start of a project.

passages.title: Food Packaging and Consumer Choices
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of consumer science, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Packaging can protect food from damage and contamination during transport. Whether a package is recyclable depends partly on local facilities.
Different label formats can make comparisons between products difficult. Small packages can require more packaging material for each unit of product.
Reusable containers may need to be used many times before their impacts are lower. The way consumers sort and discard packaging influences what happens next.
A compostable label does not necessarily mean a package can break down in a home compost bin. Packaging designers balance product protection, price and environmental impact.

passages.title: How Archaeologists Date Finds
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of archaeology, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Stratigraphy examines the sequence of soil and material layers at a site. Radiocarbon dating is used on material that was once alive.
The location and association of an object can be as informative as the object itself. Contamination can affect dating measurements and must be considered.
Dating techniques are useful over different periods and for different materials. Calibration helps translate radiocarbon measurements into calendar-date estimates.
Researchers may compare several samples to test whether results agree. Archaeological dates are often reported with an uncertainty range.
